subject: Model-7Q p95 degradation — decision: rollback or emergency traffic split
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@pinebridge.com>

Cc: ops_lead@pinebridge.com, procurement@pinebridge.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spike for Model-7Q in prod — immediate action requested

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing a sustained p95 latency spike across our production traffic for model-7Q starting ~08:40 PDT this morning. Symptoms: p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~980ms, error rate stayed low, throughput nominal. This coincided with a deploy on the Redwood side around 08:30 that moved traffic to the new compiled kernel set (per our incident window).

Attached are our initial request traces and representative request IDs (model7q-logs-0824.csv). This is impacting two high-sla endpoints used by our risk scoring pipeline — our downstream windows are starting to queue. We need one of the following immediately:

- Temporary rollback to the previous model variant (v6) for 90 minutes while you triage; OR
- Emergency traffic split (75% v6 / 25% v7) + route-based pin for worst-case customers.

Please advise the fastest path. Procurement is copied to track potential SLA carveouts if we need to escalate.

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Operations
Pinebridge Capital

Naomi / team / Sanjay — quick technical summary from on-call:

- Root correlation: increased attention context lengths from a subset of Pinebridge routes triggered a compilation path on the new kernel set. That path degrades for sequences with long KV cache churn in model-7Q; p50 unaffected, p95 and above significantly worse.
- Error rate remains low, so this is a latency regression not correctness.
- Mitigations evaluated:
  1) Full rollback to variant v6 (previous, stable kernels) — low risk, immediate, expected p95 restoration within ~5 minutes post-rollback. Token billing continues as normal.
  2) Emergency traffic split (75% v6 / 25% v7) — reduces customer impact but still leaves some exposure; requires routing config + pinned keys and takes ~10–15 minutes to ramp.
  3) Hotfix compilation toggle (kernel selector fallback) — needs infra change and ~2–3 hours to validate in prod.

Recommendation: Approve a provisional rollback to v6 for a 2-hour window (start now), followed by a controlled rollforward once we disable the problematic kernel path and validate on canary. I’ll prepare runbook steps (p95-playbook.pdf) and the rollback commands.

Attachments: p95-playbook.pdf

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Service Reliability, Redwood Inference
